# Brief — paper-kpop

**Status:** FROZEN — S1c pilot brief. Do not edit after scaffolding.
**Director:** Paper Studio, creative owner
**Frozen:** 2026-10-26
**Style id:** paper-kpop

This is a style brief, not a content brief. It describes the look and motion of the style. Names, dates, places, song words and performance content arrive later in a content brief; the style never invents them.

## 1. Occasion and audience

A short creator music video, a song drop, a tour or release announcement, or a vertical Short. It is watched first on a phone with sound off, then again with sound on. The audience is a pop audience: they scroll fast, they recognise craft, and they can tell a template from a performance.

## 2. Story in one sentence

A hand-cut paper stage assembles itself around a performer, changes shape on the beat, and detonates into colour.

## 3. Cast and faces

Up to two articulated paper performers. The lead is the hero; the second is a foil, a witness or a partner in the choreography. Faces are drawn flat and graphic, with cut hair, simple eyes and a visible joint language. A performer is built from layers, not modelled in 3D. There is no photographic likeness, no stock-photo smile and no talking head.

## 4. Shape and length

Three shapes: a 16:9 song cut, 45 seconds and 14 shots; a 9:16 Short, 30 seconds and 8 shots; and a 9:16 six-shot application at 30 seconds for a blind reuse test. The shortest shot is 1.2 seconds. Roles repeat; the pace is set by the beat, not by a fixed shot length. A 9:16 frame is re-staged, never cropped from the 16:9 composition.

## 5. Feeling

Loud, witty, handmade and kinetic. A pop stage built on a craft table: precise cutting, cheap materials, expensive timing. It should feel like the paper is performing, not like a video of paper. The humour is dry and graphic, never cute.

## 6. Anti-feeling

Never a glossy 3D render. Never a gold-foil wedding invitation. Never a clean vector explainer. Never a scrapbook of nostalgia. Never a children's craft project. Never a generic template with a paper texture laid over it. If it starts to feel soft, sentimental or software-made, it has failed.

## 7. Material and palette

Warm cream paper, dark ink, tomato red, cobalt blue, acid yellow-green and one rotating accent. Paper fibre, torn edges, halftone dots and a hard misregistered type shadow are the finish. At most four colours in a frame. Gold, pink and mint are accents, not extra roles. No gloss, no foil, no gradient mesh, no photoreal material.

## 8. Type and words

Anton for display, Archivo Black for body and stickers, DM Mono for labels, timecode and HUD, Permanent Marker for the monogram. Type is huge, stacked and treated as a paper object with a cream edge and an ink shadow. Eight words maximum per content slot. Twelve pixels minimum at 390 px. No fourth family, no soft serif, no all-caps paragraph and no lyric wall.

## 9. Motion and pace

An 88 BPM grid with a 0.21 second offset and a four-beat bar. Cuts land on the beat. The native moves are a paper snap, a sticker slam, a stacked type drop, a stage orbit, a lateral chase and a diorama pull-back. Camera moves are push-in, pull-back, pan, tilt, orbit and static; no handheld and no wobble. Transitions are cut, iris, wipe and hold; no dissolve. Paper squashes, overshoots and anticipates, then settles. The director chooses whether paper casts a contact shadow (collage) or sits flat with only the type shadow (print).

## 10. Sound

Electronic pop: synth bass, brass stabs, clipped drums, vocal chops and a bright top line. Foley is paper: a snap, a tear, a slap, a whoosh. Silence is allowed one beat before a drop. The style supplies no audio files; music and voice are cleared per film. Delivery loudness belongs to the format.

## 11. Refusals

No glossy 3D, bevel, chrome render or soft studio light. No gold foil, lace, serif wedding type or ceremonial layout. No dissolve, no camera shake, no handheld drift. No photographic faces or pasted photographs. No more than two performers. No more than four colours in a frame. No gradient mesh, airbrush or clean vector illustration. No more than eight words in a content slot. No full-frame lyric wall. No cute children's craft. No style that needs a renderer before it can be judged.

## 12. Tier and proof

Signature tier. Proven by `style:check` REVIEWABLE with no hard failures and one open director choice (`paper-shadow`); a 2×2 resolve across two briefs and two formats; a sealed blind application at 30 seconds, 9:16 and six shots with the pack unchanged; the card at 900×700 and on a 390 px phone; and three post-build critics at 9/10 GO. Proof frames: open, portrait and close across 16:9 and 9:16. No renderer and no video in S1c.
